beats.story: Even though the promise of mountains of kabob could normally make me do questionable acts, dread sits heavy in my chest. After I left work, my head was tight and hot. I drafted a cancellation text to Mom, but right before hitting send, an image of her explaining my absence popped in my head, and I couldn't pull the trigger. When I pull open the brass handle of the creaky wooden door of House of Shiraz, I'm greeted by the savory smell of dozens of khoobideh skewers roasting over a flame grill. A mix of affection and angst builds inside me as their signature big hairdos and bright blouses draw my gaze. Dinner with my mom and all my aunties is sort of like being in a hospital: you don't want to be there, but you could die if you leave. I normally try to limit my interactions with the clan to five mandatory occasions a year, making this visit rogue and dangerous. I inhale as I make my way over to their lively table.
beats.story_cn: 尽管堆积如山的烤肉串承诺通常能让我做出些不理智的举动，但沉甸甸的惶惑感仍坠在胸口。下班后，我的脑袋又紧又热。我给母亲拟了条取消约会的短信，就在即将点击发送的瞬间，脑中浮现她向亲戚们解释我缺席的场景，终究还是没按下那个键。推开“设拉子之家”吱呀作响的木门，黄铜门把传来的触感里，数十串科巴德烤肉在焰火上嘶响的咸香扑面而来。当那些标志性的蓬松卷发与明艳衬衫撞入眼帘时，某种糅合着亲昵与焦躁的情绪在胸腔翻涌。和母亲及所有姑姨共进晚餐，大抵像住院治疗——你不愿留在此地，但擅自离开可能小命不保。平日我总设法将与这族人的交集限定在每年五次“必修场合”，此番造访简直像场危险的叛逃。我深吸一口气，朝她们喧闹的餐桌走去。

beats.story: My first mistake was not packing a change of pants. The ones I'm wearing are wrinkled from a day of sitting in an office, and as I make my way over it's like a runway of shame to a row of harsh judges. Aunty Miriam spots me first and gives me a look that's somehow proud and disapproving at the same time. Aunty Miriam is the only aunty here who's actually my aunt. In the Persian aunty network, there's a series of women in every corner of the world who are either vaguely related to me or close family friends. If I were to vacation in Antarctica, my mom would tell me to check in with an aunty there or face certain public shaming. Today Aunty Miriam is sporting aggressively dark eyeshadow and a designer handbag that's so sleek and sharp, it could be wielded as a weapon. She nudges my mom, who is seated beside her, and mutters something -- a lovely comment about me, I'm sure.
beats.story_cn: 我第一个失误是没带换洗衣裤。身上这条已被办公室的椅子坐皱成咸菜干，此刻走向餐桌的步伐活像踏上通往严厉评审席的耻辱T台。米丽亚姆姑妈最先发现我，投来的眼神竟同时饱含嘉许与挑剔——她是这里唯一血缘上真正的姑妈。在波斯姑妈关系网里，地球每个角落都分布着与我有模糊亲缘或家族深交的女性。哪怕我到南极度假，母亲也会叮嘱我向当地某位姑妈报到，否则必遭公开羞辱。今日米丽亚姆姑妈挥洒着极具攻击性的深色眼影，手提包锋利得像件定制兵器，利刃般削过空气。她用手肘碰了碰身旁落座的母亲，低声嘟囔了几句——想必是些关于我的“美誉”。

beats.story: Mom yells, "Jolene, come sit," as if I were planning on going to the kitchen and showing my nips to the chef if not for her direction. Roya, the one Mom can stand the least, raises her newly threaded eyebrows as she spots me. The ground below me seems to warp as I make my way over to the one available chair at the head of the table. Silence sweeps over the party. Mom is sitting on my right, Parvin on my left, then Miriam and Roya beside them, respectively. A waiter is heading to the table beside us, but before he can get there, Mom directs him in Farsi to get me a mint yogurt drink, her lips sticky with thick, waxy lipstick. His helmet of shiny hair bobs in acknowledgment, yet his hands ball into little fists as he heads back to the bar. "Mom, I could've waited.
beats.story_cn: 妈妈喊着：“乔琳，过来坐。”仿佛若不听她安排，我就要溜进厨房向厨师展示乳头似的。罗雅——那个妈妈最看不惯的家伙，挑着新纹的眉毛瞥见我。走向餐桌主位唯一空椅时，脚下的地板似乎都在扭曲。派对瞬间沉寂。妈妈坐我右边，帕尔文在左边，接着是米丽亚姆和罗雅依次排列。一个侍者正要走向邻桌，妈妈却抢先用波斯语吩咐他给我来杯薄荷酸奶饮品，她那涂着厚重蜡质口红的嘴唇黏糊糊地动着。侍者顶着盔甲般闪亮的头发点头应承，转身走向吧台时双手却攥成了小拳头。“妈妈，其实我可以等的。”

beats.story: I don't want my food to come with spit." She flicks her perfectly manicured nails my way. "It's okay, we're Persian." This is Mom's defense for most things that my dad and I question. The waiter places the drink down in front of me. As soon as the cool, perfectly salted, minty perfection hits my tongue, something in my soul lights up. All the women at the table stare at me, not unlike predators stalking their prey. Parvin speaks first. "It's nice to finally see you, Jolene joon." Crow's-feet pull at the corners of her eyes. She's my favorite aunty.
beats.story_cn: “我可不想我的食物里附带‘加料’。”她朝我的方向精准地弹了弹她完美修饰的指甲。“没事，我们是波斯人。”这是对我爸和我大多数质疑的标准式辩护。侍者将饮品放在我面前。当那冰凉、咸淡适中、薄荷醇香的完美液体触及舌尖，我灵魂深处有什么东西被点燃了。满桌的女人齐刷刷地盯着我，那眼神活像捕食者锁定猎物。帕尔文先开口：“真高兴终于见到你，我亲爱的乔琳。”她的眼角堆起细密的鱼尾纹。她是我最喜欢的阿姨。

beats.story: She lived with us when she first moved from Iran. She'd watch stuff like Jersey Shore to learn English and write down the words she didn't understand. The ones my mom couldn't translate would often be my job. Spending my early teen years explaining words like "quiff" to an innocent older lady may have affected my development in some way. She continues: "Have you been busy? How come you never talk in the group chat?" "Oh, I think I need to update my app." I chase the straw with my mouth. If there's some FBI guy assigned to monitoring that group chat, his life has likely lost all meaning. All day long, aunties and cousins send each other: Hello Beautiful.
beats.story_cn: 她刚从伊朗搬来时，和我们同住。她会看《泽西海岸》这类节目学英语，把不懂的词记下来。我妈妈翻译不了的那些，通常就归我负责。在我青春期早期，向一位纯真的老太太解释“quiff”这类词，可能在某种层面上影响了我的成长。她继续说道：“最近很忙吗？怎么群里都不说话？”“哦，我觉得我得更新一下应用了。”我用嘴追踪着吸管。要是真有FBI探员负责监控那个群聊，他的人生估计已丧失全部意义。一整天，阿姨和表亲们都在群里互相发送：你好，美女。

[Heart GIF] [Teddy bear holding roses picture that sparkles for some reason] I don't believe there's a place for me in there, but I'm stuck and terrified that if I mute, they'll somehow sense it. beats.story: . Well, she's not a doctor." She mixes her stewed tomato into her rice and continues. "Fereshteh comes to see all of us twice a week, and she's running a big engineering project, and her kids are both in very demanding extracurriculars." Damn, Roya, fire right out the gate. I should've expected this. When I lived with my parents during my frozen-in-time years, I did everything my mom told me to do, yet I was still a big disappointment. Roya was always my loudest critic. Truthfully, I think she enjoyed making Mom feel bad that she had messed up her only child. Because according to the Aunty Way of Raising Kids, I'm a glitch in every way possible.
beats.story_cn: “反正她又不是医生。”她把炖番茄搅进米饭里，继续说，“弗蕾丝提一周来给我们看两次，还要带大项目，俩孩子课外班排得满满当天。”该死的，罗亚开场就开火。我早该料到的。当年我在家“冻结”那几年，老妈让我干嘛就干嘛，照样让她失望透顶。罗亚向来是我最响亮的批判者。说实话，她八成很享受让老妈觉得“独生女都教砸了”的快感——按阿姨们养娃的规矩，我这种存在本身就是全方位事故。

beats.story: When I lived at home, they wanted to know why I couldn't move out. When I did move to the city, Roya shifted her criticism to me leaving my family for a dead-end job, which broke a different, and slightly worse, Persian daughter code. Mom, who knows that any criticism of me is also a criticism of her, flashes me a disapproving look that lasts a millisecond, then pipes in with: "Jolene's very successful at her job. It's big national corporation, and she's about to get a promotion." Silence drapes the table as they all pause their eating to process this. The messages my colleagues sent today flash through my mind, followed by the pang of shame that I'm starting my mandatory training tomorrow. Oh, the ammo Roya would have if she only knew I was about to be laid off from a place that has a one-pancake limit during its annual rodeo breakfast. "What's your promotion?" Aunty Parvin asks. "Aren't you a secretary?" I mean, if the Supershops Apricot Body Wash gift pack Gregory gives me every Administrative Professionals' Day is right, then yeah, I'm technically a secretary.
beats.story_cn: 在家时他们质问为何不搬出去；真搬到城里了，罗亚又埋怨我为个没前途的工作抛下家庭——这又触了波斯女儿另一条，且更严苛的规矩。老妈深知对我任何批评都是在打她的脸，飞快瞥来一记不赞成的眼神，随即插话：“乔琳工作很出色呢，大企业，马上要升职了。”餐桌骤然安静，众人停筷消化这消息。今天同事发的信息闪过脑海，紧接着刺痛袭来——明天我就要开始强制培训了。天，要是罗亚知道我就要被裁员，而这家公司的年度牛仔早餐会只限吃一块煎饼，她得乐成什么样。“升什么职啊？”帕尔文阿姨问，“你不是秘书吗？”话说得没错，格雷戈里每年行政人员日送我那套超级商店杏子沐浴露礼盒就是证据——按技术定义，我确实是个秘书。

beats.story: I'm not about to admit that to Parvin. Her son is an actual doctor who specializes in something like noses and ears. Mom looks at me, pleading. So I say, "I'm currently an administrative technician, but will likely be given a supervisory position." Mom beams. "She's been getting more and more responsibilities, and a lot of people rely on her." I try not to let the plastic smile I've put on crack. "Yeah, I believe I'll soon be designing how we run certain departments, once I'm given my new role." Mom smiles. Well, it's a very quick pull of her lips, but it's there. And as she stirs her cucumber yogurt into her rice, head just a little higher, I really wish my words were true.
beats.story_cn: 我才不会在帕尔文面前承认这点。她儿子可是专攻耳鼻喉科的真·医生。母亲用眼神恳求我开口。于是我硬着头皮说：“目前担任行政技术员，但即将晋升主管。”母亲顿时眉开眼笑。“她承担的职责越来越多，很多人都指望着她呢。”我竭力维持嘴角僵硬的弧度。“没错，等新任命下来，我很快就要负责设计部门运营架构了。”母亲笑了——虽然只是唇角极快地一扬，但确实在她把黄瓜酸奶拌进米饭时，那微扬的脖颈弧度让我真心希望，刚才吹的牛能成真。

"It's not good to only worry about work. You're thirty-three now. Time is running out for kids. Are you seeing anyone?" I cough into my drink. There's no way I'd ever be able to take care of a tiny human life when I've killed plants faster than Armin without trying -- Rhonda was right to kidnap Joey. Mom's knuckles are white from balling her hands into fists around her napkin.
beats.story_cn: 我若真能升职，而她真能在这群人面前炫耀，够她得意整整十年。米里亚姆姨妈咽下最后一口藏红花鸡，皱起眉头：“只顾工作可不行。你都三十三了，生孩子的时间不等人。有对象了吗？”我呛得猛咳。连植物都养死得比阿尔敏还快（尽管不是故意的）的人，哪照顾得了小生命——朗达绑架乔伊确实是明智之举。母亲攥着餐巾的指关节已泛白。

beats.story: If these dinners are painful for me, they're even worse for her. But I know why she keeps coming. Back in Mountain Valley, before everything with me happened, she'd fought hard to climb up the ladder of the Horticulture Society, which was no small feat in a small town in Alberta, Canada, in the '90s. She even won Best Front Garden two seasons in a row. With that many old white ladies in charge, she was hanging on only by a thread. Then our lives imploded, and she was basically ghosted by them all. I heard her complain to Dad that she'd go to meetings, and they'd literally ignore her when she spoke. She even had somebody she'd conversed with hundreds of times comment that her accent was too thick to understand.
beats.story_cn: 若说这些聚餐令我如坐针毡，对她而言更是酷刑。但我明白她为何仍要坚持出席。当年在山谷镇，我家出事之前，她曾在园艺协会的阶梯上奋力攀爬——在九十年代加拿大阿尔伯塔省的小镇里，这绝非易事。她甚至连续两季斩获“最佳前院花园”殊荣。在那群掌权的老派白人太太圈子里，她本就如履薄冰。后来我们家天翻地覆，她几乎被整个圈子彻底拉黑。我听她向父亲抱怨，参加聚会发言时，众人竟会当她是空气。甚至有个曾与她深谈过数百次的人，竟说她口音太重根本听不懂。

beats.story: That was when her gardening stopped. At least here in Calgary she has friends again, even if all the aunties talk about is their kids -- every single one happy, with real career-type jobs and actual families, houses, cars, and alive plants. My mom needs a community, just like she needs a better daughter. All the aunties shift sideways to glance between me and Mom. I practically crumble when I say, "I haven't been focused on dating much, but will start to soon." I can't actually imagine dating anyone for more than one night. But unfortunately, all the aunties' eyes widen. Aunty Miriam claps her hands, clacking all the rings and her fancy old- lady watch together. "Your mommy has been waiting for this.
beats.story_cn: 那之后她便不再侍弄花草。至少在卡尔加里她重新有了朋友，尽管阿姨们谈论的无非是子女——个个生活美满，拥有正经职业、家庭、房宅、汽车，连盆栽都生机勃勃。我母亲需要这样的社群，正如她需要一个更好的女儿。阿姨们纷纷侧目，目光在我与母亲之间游移。说出“我最近没太专注约会，不过很快就会开始”时，我几乎要散架。我其实无法想象与谁约会超过一夜。可不幸的是，所有阿姨们的眼睛都亮了起来。米里亚姆阿姨拍手相庆，指间的老式名贵腕表叮当作响：“你妈可等这话好久了。”

beats.story: There are so many eligible bachelors." Good god, I've set off a terrible alarm. The aunty dating arrangement call is possibly the most precarious situation to be in. But the worst offender, my mom, calls over the waiter again, and her Farsi is too fast for me to track. Maybe she's ordering champagne to celebrate me saying I want to date? It's when Mom points at me that my heart stops. Roya laughs and says, "Oh, your mom's so excited she's asking the waiter if he's single." "She isn't?" I ask, even though I know the answer. All the guilt I had about hurting Mom dissolves like it always does at some point in our interactions, and I remember exactly why I moved away. I shouldn't have come here.
beats.story_cn: “优质单身汉那么多呢。”老天，我捅了马蜂窝。这场“相亲热线”堪称最凶险的修罗场。而罪魁祸首——我妈，竟又召来侍应生，她的波斯语快得我跟不上节奏。莫非是要开香槟庆祝我终于想通要约会？当她指向我时，我心跳骤停。罗娅笑出声：“你妈妈兴奋得在问侍应生是不是单身呢。”“不是吗？”我明知故问。所有伤害母亲的负罪感如往常那样在母女交锋中消散，我忽然记起当初离家的真正原因——本不该来的。

beats.story: As the waiter leaves, I pretend to take a bite of food as I grit through my teeth, "Mom, you didn't just ask the waiter out for me, did you?" Mom keeps her lips even: "He's in school for engineering, and his mom owns this restaurant. He's very good catch." The small bite of perfectly tender chicken in my mouth turns dry. "Did he just turn me down?" Mom pats my hand. "Don't worry, I asked him if he had friends who would like you. He promised he'd let me know." I'm obviously not interested in him either, but I could've done without the unsolicited rejection. Roya laughs. "Oh, Leila, when my Fereshteh was looking for a husband, she didn't have to look, there was line around the block." "That's great," I say, wondering if I can dissolve into this gold-painted chair. What else could one really say to that?
beats.story_cn: 侍者刚转身离开，我假装夹起食物，咬着牙低声道：“妈，您该不会是替我约了那侍者吧？”母亲双唇抿成直线：“他学工程的，他妈妈是这家餐厅老板，妥妥的优质潜力股。”口中那口嫩滑鸡肉骤然干涩。“所以……刚才算是被拒了？”母亲轻拍我的手：“别担心，我问他有没有适合你的朋友，他答应会牵线。”我自然也对他毫无兴趣，但这记当头棒喝来得实在多余。罗雅笑出声：“哎呀莱拉，我家费蕾丝泰特当年选婿，门口可排着长队呢。”“真棒，”我说，只盼能融化进这把鎏金椅中。这种时候还能接什么话？

She closes her eyes and proudly displays her eyeshadow that's more Beetlejuice than juiced beetles. "Want me to help you with your makeup?" Mom leans in closer and whispers, "You didn't take your time on your eyeliner. It's crooked. I told you to make sure to do good job." The conversation switches to heated Farsi. Arguing fingers point at my face, my hair, my boobs -- and based on the expressions, they're assessing how dire my desirability is. This isn't meant to be as hurtful as it feels.
beats.story_cn: 米里亚姆插话：“你这么漂亮又温柔，咱们只要让人见识你的美貌就行。我化妆手艺可好了，是吧？”她闭上眼得意展示着那堪比甲壳虫汁的眼影，“要我帮你化妆吗？”母亲凑近些压低声音：“你这眼线都没画好，歪歪扭扭的。早跟你说了要认真点。”对话骤然切换成激烈的波斯语。指指点点的手势对准我的脸、我的头发、我的身材——从表情判断，他们正在评估我婚恋市场的惨淡行情。这本无伤人之意，奈何痛感真切。

options.fullOutcomeStory: An impulsive burst of stress led to a bizarre remark that echoed through the quiet office. You immediately regretted speaking without filtering.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 一阵压力下的冲动爆发，催生出怪异的言论，在寂静的办公室里久久回荡。你立刻为自己口不择言而懊悔。

beats.story: It's honestly just the weirdest display of love. But I need to pull in the reins. "I can't commit to any makeovers. I have to focus on getting this promotion before I can do anything else." "Good girl." Mom pats my shoulder with one hand as the other reaches for the bowl of sabzi. "A stable job is very important. And you can always move in with me if you want to save money for a wedding one day." They all smirk in agreement while the walls close in around me, powered by the heat of their stares. "Once you get promoted, we can work on finding you a husband," Parvin says, and they each give a single nod like they've concluded this meeting of the Sad Niece Society. In my peripheral vision, I spot the waiter and a colleague crouching together while pretending not to look at me.
beats.story_cn: 说真的，这简直是爱的诡异展示。但我必须踩住刹车。"我没法承诺参与什么形象改造计划。在考虑其他事情之前，我得专注于争取晋升。""真是乖孩子。"母亲一只手拍拍我的肩膀，另一只手伸向萨布兹沙拉碗。"稳定的工作至关重要。要是你将来想攒钱办婚礼，随时可以搬来和我住。"众人露出心照不宣的假笑，而她们投来的目光汇成热浪，令四壁仿佛向我挤压收拢。"等你升了职，我们就可以帮你物色对象了，"帕尔温说道。她们每人郑重颔首，仿佛这场"悲惨侄女协会"的会议已圆满落幕。余光瞥见服务员和一位同事蹲在不远处，假装没在偷看我。

options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 乔琳始终保持清醒，选择体察同侪隐秘的困境并给予真诚共情。她凭借敏锐的机智与谨慎的周旋，在未暴露真实意图的情况下化解了这个紧张时刻。

beats.story: I take another skewer from the platter since I'll never be eating here again. At least I can leave this restaurant. At least when I walk out the door, this specific misery will end, and I can get myself a family pack of Kit Kats and go home and be alone. If I lose my job, I'll have to move in with Mom again, and there'll be no escaping any of this.
beats.story_cn: 我又从餐盘里抽出一串烤串——反正再也不会来这家餐厅了。至少我能摔门离开这鬼地方。至少走出门后，这具体的苦难就能告一段落，我可以去买一盒家庭装奇巧巧克力，回家独自呆着。如果丢了工作，就只能搬回去和老妈同住，那时可真叫无处可逃了。
